result: In 641 PACE participants non-serious adverse events (median 4) did not differ between arms (P=.47); clinically important physical-function deterioration occurred in 25% after APT, 9% CBT, 11% GET and 18% SMC.
reason: Secondary PACE safety/deterioration analysis; adds harms data to the PACE finding, not an independent cohort

result: Salivary cortisol awakening response was significantly lower in 108 adolescent CFS patients than 38 healthy peers, correlated with sleep, and normalised in those who recovered (adjusted OR 1.93 per SD rise).
reason: Independent adolescent cohort, same measure (salivary CAR), same direction

result: Systematic review of 23 case-control studies: after exercise CFS patients show larger C4a rises, enhanced oxidative stress with delayed antioxidant response and increased leukocyte IL-10/TLR4 mRNA, but no difference in circulating cytokines.
reason: Review, not an independent cohort; its gene-expression evidence is the Light lab data already cited; better fits the broad exaggerated immune response to exercise finding

result: Systematic review of 23 case-control studies concluded exercise provokes a more pronounced complement C4a split-product response in CFS than in sedentary controls (level B evidence).
reason: Review summarising the Sorensen C4a studies already cited; no new cohort, so not a replication

result: In the prospective cohort of 300+ adolescents after infectious mononucleosis, baseline autonomic symptoms and days in bed since IM were the only significant predictors of meeting CFS criteria at 6 months in stepwise regression.
reason: Same Chicago post-mono adolescent cohort; adds risk-factor analysis

result: After IM in adolescents, acute-illness severity markers (days in bed, autonomic symptoms) predicted CFS at 6 months while stress, life events, family stress and psychiatric disorder did not once autonomic symptoms were controlled.
reason: Supports acute severity, not psychological factors, predicting post-infective fatigue in a separate adolescent EBV cohort; no cytokine data

result: 50 CFS vs 50 controls reported more cognitive problems but did not differ on CVLT, Rey figure, PASAT or Stroop; subjective and objective scores were uncorrelated and depression related to subjective complaints.
reason: Tests the same objective attention/memory measures and finds no group difference

result: On a 20-minute standing test in 306 CFS clinic patients, 11% (33/306) met POTS criteria (HR rise >30 bpm); CFS-POTS patients were younger and haemodynamically distinct, and HR variability was linked to fatigue.
reason: Adds a prevalence estimate within the 6-43% range with a stand protocol and an age effect

result: POTS comorbidity was 11% (33/306) on a 20-minute standing task in an Australian CFS clinic.
reason: Does not measure cerebral blood flow or preload, the core of this finding; prevalence is covered by the neuro-pots-prevalence link

result: PACE investigators' recovery analysis at 52 weeks: trial-defined recovery in 22% after CBT and GET vs 8% APT and 7% SMC (OR about 3.4-3.7).
reason: Same PACE trial, not an independent cohort; it is the recovery analysis later disputed by the Wilshire re-analysis
